prompt:
Use case: illustration-story
Asset type: Empire C01-SCENE-REFUGEE-BRIDGEWORK, a complete opaque 16:9 narrative illustration, target 1672 by 941 pixels.
Primary request: Refugees and engineers repairing a modest river bridge together. In the central foreground an adult refugee in patched brown travel clothes and an engineer in ochre leather work apron and brown rounded work helmet are doing equal physical work, both guiding the same thick replacement timber down onto the bridge's solid crossbeams. Their hands actually support the timber and their attentive faces turn toward the work and each other. Both stand securely on an intact area of the deck. The repair action is calm practical cooperation, chosen freely. An additional adult engineer kneels on secure boards to fit a wooden wedge at a joint; two civilian helpers bring a coil of rope or sort timber on the nearby bank. No named story hero is depicted.
Source meaning: This canonical everyday scene is specifically refugees and engineers working together on a bridge. The original slot has a mixed timber-and-stone bridge over a blue stream, workers and civilians, repair planks, rope and tools on both banks. Preserve that subject while rebuilding it as a close, readable narrative view. Do not turn it into the separate night-time White River escape or combat scene, and do not show labor enforced by soldiers.
Input images: Images 1, 2 and 3 are approved CH06-S29, CH04-S19 and CH07-S36E STYLE references only. Do not copy their named characters, ghosts, dragon, insignia or story props. Image 4 is approved ordinary engineer unit DESIGN reference: ochre apron, cream sleeves, blue-green shoulder fabric, rounded brown helmet, work gloves and tool belt. Image 5 is ordinary adult refugee DESIGN reference: brown patched outer garment, grey shirt, plain boots, dark hair and a travel bundle. These last two establish ordinary role design, not named identities; adapt proportions to the narrative references.
Scene: A small broad stream and a low practical timber bridge built on rough stone piers. Show intact span, a short clearly visible section under repair and thick replacement boards so the action reads instantly. Simplify the structure into few coherent beams. On the bank, a modest handcart and travel bundles establish the refugee group without crowding. A few broad rocks, green and ochre trees and distant hills complete the opaque environment.
Style/medium: Closely match the accepted references' chunky matte cartoon-fantasy illustration, strong clean dark silhouettes, broad simple color masses, compact sturdy figures, simplified rounded faces, generous readable hands, 2 to 3 shadow values, little texture. No stippling, hatching, realistic microtexture, gloss, photorealism or tiny isometric map view.
Composition: One wide edge-to-edge full scene, no border or collage. Slightly elevated close narrative camera shows the deck, central joined repair effort and water below. Keep both main faces and their shared timber action grouped in the central 35 percent of the canvas so they remain readable at 256 by 144. Give both central workers similar visual importance. Side helpers are smaller and secondary. The river remains clearly visible without becoming a giant dangerous chasm.
Mood and palette: Clear daylight, practical concentration with a little mutual warmth. Matte warm timber and ochre work gear, ordinary brown and cream civilian clothes, blue-green river and a soft blue sky.
Constraints: Entirely opaque. No flags or heraldry, no invented star/snowflake/crown/sigil, no written text or symbols, no watermark, no UI. No named heroes, no weapons in use, no supervisor directing from above, no chained people, no forced labor, no kneeling submission, no children laboring, no battle, magic, fire, dragon or ghosts. All work gestures and bridge beams must be structurally coherent and easy to read.
